pr: between PR3 merge and PR4 (one-shot migration; not a PR)
title: etl4/scripts/migrate_partition_ym.py -- zero-reprocess monolith -> ym partitions
objective: Rechunk each existing <table>/part.parquet monolith into <table>/ym=YYYY-MM/part.parquet partitions via pyarrow streaming (iter_batches), per architecture section 6. Zero re-processing of upstream data. Row-count equality gate pre/post. Idempotent. Emit pipeline_watermarks rows at the end. Print Postgres-side migration SQL block to stdout; do NOT run it.
status_reason: Architecture section 6 PARTITIONED_TABLES is unexecutable for 3 of 7 tables on the current data: link_flight_aircraft and link_flight_route have no 'day' column in their monolith, and sat_flight_summary's firstseen key disagrees with the T-08 writer's file-month key (~12.7k rows cross month boundaries, dry-run confirmed). The script delivered IS correct for the 4 remaining tables (hub_flight, sat_state_observation, fact_flight, fact_trajectory_enriched) and flags the 3 gaps with actionable diagnostics instead of silently migrating to a split-brain state. Data-engineer needs to decide on the key alignment for the 3 flagged tables before T-13 can approve a production migration pass.

contract_deviations: ARCHITECTURE SECTION 6 GAP #1 (link_flight_aircraft, link_flight_route): both monoliths lack the 'day' column that architecture section 6 PARTITIONED_TABLES assigns as the ym source. Confirmed via pq.read_schema. load_dt is a single ingest timestamp; filename on link_flight_aircraft is shard enumeration (part-NNN.parquet), not the bronze source. Script reports schema_mismatch and continues. Options for data-engineer: (a) extend raw_vault._build_link_* to emit 'day' into the link schema, then re-run T-08 to regenerate the monolith with day present; (b) add a join-against-hub_flight fallback (loading 93M hk_flight->day pairs is ~3.5 GB of memory -- out of scope for a one-shot script); (c) accept that link tables are rebuilt from flightlist bronze rather than migrated (NOT zero-reprocess but may be acceptable for links which are tiny compared to sat_state_observation).

ARCHITECTURE SECTION 6 GAP #2 (sat_flight_summary): architecture maps firstseen -> ym_from_epoch (section 6), but (a) the production monolith stores firstseen as timestamp[ns, tz=UTC] not int64, so ym_from_epoch would fail its astype('Int64') cast; and (b) T-08's writer keys sat_flight_summary partitions by the FLIGHTLIST BRONZE FILE MONTH, not firstseen. Dry-run confirms the mismatch: 6,152 of 2022-06's 2,454,119 rows land in 2022-05 and 6,533 of 2022-12's 2,146,527 land in 2022-11 if firstseen is used. Migrating with firstseen would hide these rows from any per-ym mart join AND duplicate them on a rewind+rebuild (T-08 would recreate them under the file-month key). Flagged as unsupported_reason until data-engineer picks one key for both migration and T-08 (candidates: lastseen if it aligns 100% with file-month, hub_flight.hk_flight -> day lookup).

schema_mismatch policy: (dry-run) WARN, exit 0; (real run) FAIL, exit 1 + skip watermark seeding. Advisor note: a real run that silently migrates 4 tables and skips 3 would seed a half-baked state. Operator must pass --tables explicitly to run the supported subset.

Monolith NOT deleted post-migration (per dispatch + architecture section 6 close); operator deletes manually after verifying partition reads. Exit condition documented in operator_runbook step 4 (vault_io.row_count(name) must equal pre-migration monolith footer count).
under_specification_resolved: 'Postgres-side migration' output format: stdout only; POSTGRES_SQL_BLOCK module constant; operator pipes to psql when ready
SQL block timezone: added SET LOCAL TIME ZONE 'UTC' inside BEGIN so to_char(to_timestamp(...)) aligns with ym_from_epoch (both UTC)
pipeline_runs.ym ADD CONSTRAINT: NOT re-emitted (already in create_tables.sql T-01B, grep-confirmed at lines 155-205)
schema_mismatch vs row_count_mismatch exit codes: schema is informational in dry-run (WARN exit 0) and fatal in real run (FAIL exit 1); row_count_mismatch is always fatal

In-file 'ym' column: migrated partitions get `ym` appended inside each file body so the schema matches T-08 output (raw_vault.py line 543); without this, readers concat partitioned + monolith shapes and get NaN ym for every migrated row
_DONE sentinel: dropped beside part.parquet after commit, mirroring raw_vault._write_done, so T-08 and T-10 treat migrated partitions as resumed and do not rebuild over them
--skip-watermark for offline smokes added (smoke subprocess-runs with it + env.pop('POSTGRES_DSN'))

integration_points.reads: Each <table>/part.parquet monolith via pq.ParquetFile.iter_batches(batch_size=1_000_000); vault_io.list_ym for watermark seeding; pq.read_schema for schema validation; pq.ParquetFile footer for row counts and idempotency
integration_points.writes: <table>/ym=YYYY-MM/.part.parquet.<pid>.tmp -> os.replace -> part.parquet (atomic); <table>/ym=YYYY-MM/_DONE sentinel beside each partition; pipeline_watermarks via watermark.set (layer=vault for silver, marts for gold); POSTGRES_SQL_BLOCK to stdout (not executed)
consumers: etl4.vault.vault_io.read_table reads the new ym tree transparently (partition > monolith fallback)
etl4.vault.marts (T-14) reads vault tables via vault_io.read_table
etl4.vault.postgres_sink (T-17) reads gold marts tables via vault_io.read_table
etl4.vault.raw_vault._partition_done (T-08) treats migrated partitions as done because _DONE is present
etl4.run_e2e drift check (T-22) compares vault_io.list_ym vs pipeline_watermarks.last_ym

risks_known_limits: link_flight_aircraft / link_flight_route / sat_flight_summary migration paths are unresolved (contract_deviations #1-#2). BLOCKER for the operator on those three tables. For sat_flight_summary: a subsequent T-08 flightlist write with a cleared watermark would create ym dirs using the file-month key; vault_io.read_table would then concat the (hypothetical firstseen-keyed) migrated partitions with the (file-month-keyed) T-08 partitions and the result would be wrong. SAFE PATH: do NOT migrate these three tables until data-engineer closes the gap.
Memory footprint during real migration: one 1M-row batch in memory per table pass; peak RSS bounded by pyarrow's batch deserialization.
Watermark seed may skip if Postgres is unreachable; script prints an informative message. Operator re-runs when Postgres is back; partitions on disk are unaffected.
Orphan tmp files from a killed process (not our abort path): `.part.parquet.<pid>.tmp` naming makes them tractable to clean (`find data -name '.part.parquet.*.tmp' -delete`).

seed_watermarks is not exercised by the smoke (which runs offline with --skip-watermark). Covered by inspection against t10_sat_smoke's watermark snapshot/restore pattern; a follow-up smoke could add a live-DB case.

Monolith is preserved post-migration (operator deletes manually after confirming vault_io.row_count == pre-migration footer). vault_io.read_table prefers partitions when both coexist; only disk pressure is at stake.

preconditions: PR2 (vault layer) and PR3 (marts layer) merged; readers route through vault_io.read_table so partition + monolith fallback both work
Disk headroom at least equal to the sum of the 4 migratable monoliths; migration doubles the on-disk footprint for migrated tables until the operator deletes monoliths
run_supported_subset: 1. Dry-run: `python -m etl4.scripts.migrate_partition_ym --dry-run`  (sanity + plan surface; exits 0 even with the 3 schema gaps WARN'd)

2. Real run on the 4 supported tables: `python -m etl4.scripts.migrate_partition_ym --tables hub_flight,sat_state_observation,fact_flight,fact_trajectory_enriched`  (writes partitions + _DONE + watermarks; prints SQL block)
3. Apply SQL: `python -m etl4.scripts.migrate_partition_ym --dry-run --tables fact_trajectory_enriched 2>/dev/null | sed -n '/---- Postgres/,/---- end SQL/p' | psql $POSTGRES_DSN`
post: 4. Verify partition reads: for each migrated table, assert `vault_io.row_count(name) == pre_migration_footer_count`; both numbers appear in the script's stdout

5. Delete monoliths (ONLY after step 4 passes): `for t in hub_flight sat_state_observation; do rm data/silver/vault/$t/part.parquet; done; for t in fact_flight fact_trajectory_enriched; do rm data/gold/marts/$t/part.parquet; done`
6. Resolve the 3 flagged schema/key gaps (contract_deviations #1-#2) before PR3 marts reads touch link tables or sat_flight_summary

exit_condition_for_monolith_delete: When vault_io.row_count(name) == pre-migration pq.ParquetFile(<name>/part.parquet).metadata.num_rows for every migrated table (steps 4+5 of operator runbook). Not before. For the 3 unsupported tables: do NOT delete their monoliths until the schema / key gap is resolved; they are the only remaining copy of those rows.
